text: The copper has six doubled letters. Written in rows of 7, five of them start in the same column.
Written in rows of 21, a pair of letters one above the other turns up twice 11 times.

Both were found by trying many widths, so the fair comparison is with shuffled coppers at their own best width. After that correction the column happens about 0.5 times in a hundred and the repeats about 1: both are real features of the copper.
